request: Imagine the black handle is a stand. Add another one on the other side of device in approximately same distane from side wall as the existing one. Remove the Cordholder. Cut the bottom of the handles so it allows the device to be stable on a flat surface.

actions.operation: Create an additional handle/stand feature (duplicate/mirror of existing handle) on the opposite side of the device

parameters.offset_from_side_wall: approximately same distance as existing handle

actions.target: Existing black handle (used as the reference for the new one); device body/side
actions.relational_constraint: Place the new handle on the other side of the device, at approximately the same distance from the side wall as the existing handle
actions.unresolved_reference: Which specific 'side wall' is used as the distance reference; what defines 'other side' (symmetry plane/center plane or opposite exterior face); exact attachment faces/edges and orientation of the handle relative to the device
Identify which body/feature in the CAD model is the 'Cordholder' and whether removal affects dependent features (fillets, ribs, holes, patterns)

actions.operation: Cut/trim the bottom of the handles to create a stable flat contact with a planar surface
actions.target: Bottom region of the handles (existing handle and the newly added handle)
actions.relational_constraint: Modify the bottom of the handles so the device can be stable on a flat surface (implies a planar cut creating flat support faces aligned to a base plane)
actions.unresolved_reference: What plane represents the 'flat surface' (e.g., global XY plane, device base face, or an assembly ground plane); how much material to remove and what contact area is required for stability (coplanarity with other bottom surfaces, number of contact points)

intention: Add a second stand/handle to support the device from both sides in a similar position relative to the side wall.
Eliminate the cordholder from the design.
Ensure the device can sit stably on a flat surface by flattening/cutting the bottoms of the handles.
